transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I came in because I just feel wound up almost all the time. It's like... my body is constantly bracing for the next bad thing to happen. And it doesn't really matter what I'm doing. I could just be sitting at my desk working, or trying to enjoy dance night, and that tense feeling is just always there.
When you feel this wound-up tension, does it come in sudden waves or episodes, or is it more of a constant background feeling throughout the day?

Um, it's definitely more of a constant background feeling. I don't really get sudden waves of it, or at least I haven't noticed it happening like that. It's just... a steady tension that kind of sits there all day.
How long have you been experiencing this constant tension feeling? Has it been going on for weeks, months, or longer?
It's been going on for months. I'd say about nine months now. It really started right around the time my condo loan began moving toward foreclosure. So, yeah, it's been a constant thing since then.

Have you had any recent medical illnesses, injuries, or changes in your medications? And are you currently taking any substances like caffeine, energy drinks, or anything else that might affect how you feel?

Um, no, nothing like that. I haven't been sick or hurt recently, and I'm not taking any medications. And as for caffeine or substances... no, I don't drink energy drinks or anything like that. I really don't take anything out of the ordinary that would make me feel this way.

During these nine months of constant tension, have you ever experienced sudden episodes where your heart started racing, you felt short of breath, or had a sense of intense fear or dread that came on quickly?

No, I haven't really had anything like that. It's just that constant tension I mentioned. I don't get those sudden, intense spikes of fear or feel like I can't breathe. It's just a steady, all-day kind of stress.
Besides worrying about your condo situation, what other things do you find yourself worrying about during these nine months? Are there multiple areas of your life that cause you concern?

Yeah, it's... it doesn't really stay on the condo anymore. It kind of jumps around to a lot of different things. Like, I'll start worrying about whether my cousin is upset with me about something, or... or I'll stress about making a mistake on a support call at work. And then it shifts to bigger things, like how I'll ever manage to save money or just move forward with my life. So, yeah, it's definitely multiple areas of my life right now.
Besides feeling tense, do you experience other physical symptoms like muscle aches, trouble sleeping, or difficulty concentrating on tasks?

Yeah, the sleep is definitely an issue. Most nights I get into bed completely exhausted, but my brain just won't shut off. It just keeps replaying things—like loan notices, or work tickets, or just worrying about things I might have missed during the day. I usually end up lying there until 2 or 3 in the morning. And even when I do finally get some sleep, I wake up feeling like I barely rested at all.
Besides the sleep trouble you mentioned, do you notice that you feel restless or on edge, or do you find yourself getting irritable more easily than usual?

Yeah, I definitely feel on edge. Honestly, that's a big part of why I came in. I just feel wound up almost all the time. It's like... like my body is constantly bracing for the next bad thing to happen. And it doesn't really matter what I'm doing—even if I'm just sitting at my desk at work, or trying to go out and enjoy dance night, I just have this restless, tense feeling that I can't seem to shake.
You mentioned your brain won't shut off at night. During the day when you're trying to work or focus on tasks, do you find it hard to concentrate or keep your attention on what you're doing?

Yeah, I do. It's actually been pretty tough at work lately. I'll be right in the middle of writing a script, or, you know, helping a user on a call—whether it's in English or Spanish—and suddenly I realize I'm just staring blankly at the screen. My mind just drifts off to all the things that could go wrong with my life, and I completely lose the thread of what I was doing. It takes a lot of effort to pull myself back and focus again.

Have there been any times during these nine months when you suddenly felt a wave of intense anxiety or fear that built up over just a few minutes, even if you couldn't point to a specific trigger at that moment?

No, not really like that. It's more of a constant, steady worry for me. I don't think I've ever had a sudden wave of intense fear out of nowhere. It's just this continuous feeling of being on edge, but it doesn't suddenly peak in a few minutes.
During these nine months, have there been any stretches of time—even a week or two—where you felt noticeably less anxious or tense, or has the worry and tension been pretty much constant throughout?
No, there really hasn't been a break. It's been pretty constant this whole time. I can't remember a week, or even a few days, where I didn't feel this way. It's just always there in the background.

When you worry about things like your cousin being upset with you or making mistakes at work, do those worries feel reasonable and proportional to what could actually happen, or do they often feel blown out of proportion even though you know logically they might not be that big of a deal?

I know they're probably blown out of proportion. Like, logically, I know my cousin isn't going to hate me forever if I can't make it to a dinner, and missing one detail on a ticket at work isn't going to get me fired on the spot. But it doesn't feel that way in the moment. The worry just feels so big and real to me, even if a part of my brain knows it's an overreaction.
